merger_name: Johns Lyng Group – C&M Build Group

acquirers.name: Johns Lyng Group (Nominee) Pty Ltd as trustee for the Johns Lyng Unit Trust

merger_description:
Johns Lyng Group (Nominee) Pty Ltd as trustee for the Johns Lyng Unit Trust, a subsidiary of Johns Lyng Group Limited (**Johns Lyng Group**), proposes to acquire 60% of the total issued shares in C&M Central Pty Ltd and 60% of the total issued unit capital of C&M Central Unit Trust (collectively, **C&M Build Group**) (the **Acquisition**).

Johns Lyng Group, via an indirect subsidiary, is ultimately majority-owned and controlled by the private equity firm Pacific Equity Partners (**PEP**). PEP is an Australian-based Private markets fund manager specialising in private equity investments across Australia and New Zealand, including through its acquisition of Johns Lyng Group in October 2025.

Johns Lyng Group’s operations in Australia comprise its core business of insurance building & restoration services, in addition to commercial building services (such as heating, ventilation and air-conditioning, floorcovering, home staging and shopfitting), strata & building management services, disaster recovery & management services and home & compliance services.

C&M Build Group is a multi-disciplined design, engineering and construction services provider, operating across Eastern Australia. C&M Build Group specialises in the provision of end-to-end construction services for the insurance, residential and commercial sectors, including restoration, construction, disaster management and related services.

Johns Lyng Group and C&M Build Group overlap in the supply of insurance building and restoration services.

events.title: Johns Lyng Group - C&M Build Group - Phase 1 Determination

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties and other
information available to it.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The merged firm would continue to face competition from
multiple providers of insurance building and restoration
services.
